The following instructions state everything you need to know in order to participate in this experiment. Please read them carefully.

By participating in this experiment you will earn a show-up fee of £1.30. Additionally, you have the chance of earning a bonus payment up to £5.00. The amount of the potential bonus payment depends on your own decisions and the decisions of other participants.

Please note that these instructions are the same for all participants in the experiment. All payments are real, and all participants are real too. All information that you receive during the experiment is truthful and real.

Your decisions during this experiment remain fully anonymous. None of the other participants will be able to link your decisions to your identity or get to know your name. The show-up fees and bonus payments will be paid out anonymously via Prolific at the end of the experiment. The other participants will not receive any information about your earnings.

Group formation

In this experiment, you will play a game in a group of four. You will play this game one time. Before the game starts, participants are randomly assigned a role: one in four participants is assigned the role of responder; the other three are assigned the role of proposers.

You will be privately informed about your role and keep this role throughout the experiment. Please remember that you will remain anonymous during the experiment. You will not get to know the identity of the other participants in your group, neither during the experiment nor after the experiment. The other participants will also not know your identity.

Short overview of decisions in the game

The game will be played in three phases.

  • In phase 1, the three proposers make two offers: an actual offer and a communicated offer.
  • In phase 2, the responder observes the communicated offers and decides whether or not to accept the set of 3 communicated offers. If the set of 3 communicated offers is rejected, the game ends. If the set of 3 communicated offers is accepted, the game moves to phase 3.
  • In phase 3, one of the 3 communicated offers is randomly selected.

More details on the rules of the game and the specific duties per role (responder or proposer) will follow now.

Decisions in the game: Proposers

In phase 1, each proposer must decide individually how to divide £5.00 between themselves and the responder. Each proposer may offer to the responder an amount between £0.00 and £5.00 (in increments of cents). If the offer is accepted, this is what the responder will actually receive. The proposer will keep the remaining money. This offer is called the actual offer and is not visible to the responder or to any of the other proposers.

After deciding on their actual offer, each proposer must also decide on an offer between between £0.00 and £5.00 (in increments of cents) that they will communicate to the responder. This communication does not have to match the actual offer. This offer is called the communicated offer. It is visible to the responder only, not to the other two proposers. The proposer whose communicated offer is randomly selected will receive a bonus payment. The proposers whose communicated offers are not randomly selected will not receive a bonus payment.

So, all proposers make two offers. One is the actual offer, which determines how the £5.00 will be divided. The second is the communicated offer. This is the offer that the responder will see when making the decision to accept or reject the set of 3 communicated offers in phase 2. In phase 3, one of the communicated offers is randomly selected.

Decisions in the game: Responders

The responder observes the communicated offers of all three proposers. In phase 2, the responder must first decide whether to accept or reject the set of 3 communicated offers. If the responder decides to reject the set of 3 communicated offers, the game ends and nobody will receive a bonus payment.

If the responder decides to accept the set of 3 communicated offers, the game proceeds to phase 3. In phase 3, one of the three communicated offers is randomly selected. The responder will share the money with the proposer whose offer is randomly selected, based on the actual offer of the proposer. Please note that the actual offer does not have to be the same as the communicated offer.

Bonus payment

If the responder rejects the set of 3 communicated offers, no bonus payment will be given to any of the participants.

If the responder accepts, only the proposer whose offer is randomly selected will receive a bonus payment of £5.00, minus the actual amount that was offered to the responder. The responder will receive the randomly selected proposer’s actual offer. Proposers that are not randomly selected will receive no bonus payment.

In phase 1, the three proposers make their offers for a division of the £5.00 bonus between themselves and the responder. They make an actual offer, which is how the money will actually be divided and they make a communicated offer, which is the offer the responder gets to see.

In phase 2, the responder observes the set of 3 communicated offers and decides whether to accept or reject this set of 3 communicated offers. If the set of 3 communicated offers is rejected, the game ends and nobody receives a bonus. If the set of 3 communicated offers is accepted, the game moves to phase 3.

In phase 3, one of the communicated offers is randomly selected. The actual offer that the randomly selected proposer has made is then implemented. The proposers that were not randomly selected will not receive a bonus.
